Every alpha decay emits a helium-4 nucle.why: The definition of alpha decay, in the first sentences of Wikipedia's Alpha decay article and in textbook form in Dolma ('an alpha particle is a helium nucleus'). It follows from nothing more basic.

sources.quote: An alpha particle is identical to the nucleus of a helium-4 atom, which consists of two protons and two neutrons.

Uranium-238 undergoes alpha decay..why: Uranium-238's alpha decay and its product are both stated by name, which is what the name worlds assume.
